articles.title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing
articles.summary: Athletes are cashing massive checks to promote sportsbooks and betting apps, blurring the line between legitimate sports figures and casino marketing arms. It matters because celebrity endorsements drive retail betting volume, which creates artificial demand spikes that prediction market operators have to hedge against in real time.

articles.title: NFLs WAGs Now Have Prediction Market Sponsorships, Too
articles.summary: The wives and girlfriends of NFL players are now landing sponsorship deals with prediction market platforms, expanding the influencer marketing playbook into crypto-adjacent betting. It's a legitimacy signal that prediction markets are graduating from fringe retail trader obsession to mainstream consumer product, like DeFi before the rug pulls.

articles.title: Commentary: Rolling the dice on prediction markets: North Carolina's warning for Indiana
articles.summary: North Carolina apparently tried something with prediction markets and it went badly enough to serve as a cautionary tale for Indiana. If states keep banning or botching their regulatory approach, the entire market infrastructure stays fragmented and risky for everyone trying to actually use these things.

articles.title: Young New Yorkers Are Losing on Kalshi, City Council Says
articles.summary: Young New Yorkers are dumping money into Kalshi's prediction markets and apparently losing it faster than they can earn it, prompting the city council to clutch its pearls. If regulators start cracking down on retail participation in prediction markets, the entire "democratizing forecasting" thesis gets a lot harder to sell.

articles.title: KKR curbs staff betting on prediction markets
articles.summary: KKR, the mega-cap private equity firm, is restricting employees from trading on prediction markets, likely citing compliance risks or conflicts of interest as the reason. When institutional heavyweights start locking down market access, it signals regulators are paying attention and forces prediction market platforms to tighten their own rules.

articles.title: US Prediction Markets: Modern Timeline
articles.summary: The US finally has a legit timeline for when prediction markets will stop operating in legal gray area and actually become regulated. That matters because right now everyone's guessing what the rules will look like, and the second they're official, the entire market structure probably shifts.

articles.title: $20,000 in Bets, $350,000 in Profit: ‘Suspicious’ Polymarket Clusters Nailed Jensen Huang’s Nvidia Return
articles.summary: Someone made $350K on a $20K bet by timing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return perfectly on Polymarket, raising fresh questions about whether certain traders have information the rest of us don't. The pattern matters because it's the kind of edge that makes prediction markets either thrillingly efficient or deeply broken depending on who's actually allowed to know what.

articles.title: After judge signals ‘steep hill’ in regulatory case, Kalshi pauses operations in Utah
articles.summary: Kalshi, a prediction market platform betting on political and economic events, hit a legal wall in Utah after a judge suggested the company faces serious obstacles in its regulatory battle. The setback signals that prediction markets still can't legally operate nationwide, keeping billions of potential bettors stuck in regulatory limbo while platforms fight state by state.

articles.title: New York judge urged Kalshi to compromise on limiting bets by anyone under 21
articles.summary: A New York judge pushed Kalshi, the CFTC-approved prediction market platform, to restrict betting access for anyone under 21 instead of fighting the age requirement outright. The move signals regulators are willing to negotiate on market access rules, which could reshape how prediction markets balance growth against compliance pressures.

articles.title: Democrats put campus gambling in the crosshairs
articles.summary: Democrats are moving to restrict or ban gambling operations on college campuses, targeting everything from sportsbooks to daily fantasy sports apps marketed to students. This matters because regulatory crackdowns on campus betting could reshape the entire college sports betting ecosystem and potentially crater some operators' growth projections if restrictions gain real traction.

articles.title: New York lawmaker proposes bill to regulate and tax prediction markets
articles.summary: A New York lawmaker wants to slap regulation and taxes on prediction markets, the latest attempt by legislators to bring America's fastest-growing betting category under government control. If it passes, expect the playbook to spread to other states like a bad rash, potentially killing the margins that make these platforms worth running in the first place.

articles.title: Top 1% of Polymarket accounts took 91% of U.S. midterm winnings, study finds
articles.summary: The top 1% of Polymarket traders scooped up 91% of the winnings from U.S. midterm bets, suggesting the platform's wealth is consolidating around a tiny cluster of sophisticated players. That concentration raises obvious questions about whether prediction markets actually aggregate crowd wisdom or just reward whoever can afford to dump the most capital at the right moment.
